generic_sampling_rules.integer: sample uniformly from the observed min..max range; include min, max, and one step inside each bound; 5% fresh values outside the observed range when no range rule forbids it
generic_sampling_rules.varchar: sample from the observed value pool; 10% near-variants (case change, trailing space, one-character edit) when no enum rule forbids it
generic_sampling_rules.char: sample from the observed value pool; 10% near-variants (case change) when no enum rule forbids it
generic_sampling_rules.primary_key: generate sequential unique values in the column's declared format; never NULL
generic_sampling_rules.foreign_key: copy from the parent table's key pool; 10% NULL when the column is nullable; 10% orphan values not present in the parent when the column is nullable
generic_sampling_rules.null: for every nullable column, 5% of rows get NULL; at least one NULL row per nullable column per instance
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: for numeric columns with a comparison-boundary target, include the literal, literal-1 and literal+1
generic_sampling_rules.tie: for ORDER columns with a tie target, ensure at least two rows share the top value
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate: for DISTINCT columns with a duplicate target, ensure 20-50% of values repeat

Execution feedback shows 20/20 valid instances, 0 FK violations, 0 PK duplicates, 0 NOT NULL violations, 0 changed compact rows, and reproducible output (returncode 0, n_fail 0).
issues.requested_revision: None blocking. Note that the specification's table_sizes_per_instance (bank 4, customer 6, loan 6) is applied as the *generated* row count per instance, not the total table size; this is consistent with the append-to-compact design and the observed rows_added (e.g. bank 30/20 ≈ 1.5, customer 96/20 ≈ 4.8, loan 67/20 ≈ 3.35 — below the nominal sizes because PK/UNIQUE dedup and NULL handling drop some rows). If exact per-instance sizes are required, the engineer should document that dedup can reduce the appended count.

issues.evidence: The NULL rule is implemented: _apply_null_rule plants at least one NULL and one non-NULL per nullable column, and fill_foreign_keys_consistently does the same for nullable FKs. Execution feedback confirms NULLs appear in every nullable column (e.g. customer.branch_ID 24/96, loan.cust_ID 23/67, loan.branch_ID 20/67), and no NOT NULL/PK column received NULL. The 'planted NULL never replaced' invariant is respected because _apply_null_rule only fills a non-NULL when all values are NULL.

The loan.branch_ID column is declared varchar(3) while bank.branch_ID is INT; the specification's uncertainty note says generation copies the string form of the parent key. fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws from the parent's values (which are ints from bank.branch_ID) and inserts them into a varchar column. SQLite is dynamically typed so this does not raise integrity errors (0 FK violations reported), but the stored values are integers in a varchar column.
issues.requested_revision: No blocking change; optionally cast parent key values to str when the child column is declared varchar, to match the declared type and the specification's stated intent.
